items.name: Embed gauntlet adversarial evaluator prompt
items.description: Author evaluators/gauntlet-eval.md with the adversarial code-review instructions and add a GauntletEval variable to evaluators/evaluators.go via //go:embed. The generated workflow script bakes this prompt as the evaluator agent's instruction per the adversarial-evaluation-gauntlet spec.

tests.description: evaluators.GauntletEval is a non-empty string at runtime — the embedded file content is accessible from the cmd package
The prompt instructs the evaluator to adversarially review code and mutate it directly to correct deficiencies against the batch's test criteria, without emitting a verdict word

items.name: Implement batch computation
items.description: Given a validated PlanJSON and batch size, produce an ordered []Batch: process layers in declared order, topologically sort items within each layer by depends_on (stable, declared order tiebreak), chunk by batch size, and number batches sequentially 1-based across all layers.

tests.description: Every plan item appears in exactly one batch across all layers
For any item, all its depends_on items appear in the same batch or an earlier-numbered batch
No batch exceeds the configured batch size; every batch has at least one item
Batches are numbered sequentially starting at 1, continuing across layer boundaries without resetting
When implementing.batch exceeds the item count in a layer, that layer produces a single batch containing all its items
A plan with a single item produces exactly one batch of one item

items.name: Derive output filename and handle collisions
items.description: Derive the workflow filename from context.domain and context.module as <domain>-<module>-impl.js, sanitized to the slash-command charset (lowercase, hyphens only). When the derived name already exists under .claude/workflows/, prepend a disambiguating prefix to produce a fresh name and log a WARN naming both the intended and chosen names.

tests.description: domain/module values containing uppercase letters and non-alphanumeric characters are sanitized to lowercase hyphen-separated output
When the derived name already exists, a new prefixed name is chosen and the original file is left byte-for-byte unchanged
A WARN line is printed when a collision is resolved, naming both the intended filename and the chosen filename

items.name: Render the workflow JavaScript script
items.description: Produce the self-contained Claude Code workflow script string from baked batches and config values: a pure-literal meta export, one phase() per batch plus an evaluate phase, a primary agent once per batch, an evaluator loop bounded by min_rounds/max_rounds with a change-detector agent each round, and commit instructions baked in only when enable_commits is true. The script must encode error recovery paths (primary null, evaluator null, git failure) and emit the required log() calls per the gauntlet spec.

tests.description: The emitted script exports a pure-literal meta object with name matching '<domain>-<module>-impl', a one-line description, and a phases array with one entry per batch plus an evaluate phase
The emitted script contains no require, import, Date.now(), Math.random(), new Date(), fs API calls, or calls to forgectl
The primary agent() call in each batch uses the baked implement.model and implement.type values from config
The evaluator loop runs at most max_rounds times and respects the min_rounds floor: a no-change round before min_rounds is reached does not end the loop
The change-detector agent uses a haiku model with Bash capability to run git and report changed/clean; it is the sole authority on convergence
When enable_commits is false, no commit instruction appears in any baked prompt (primary, evaluator, or change-detector)
The baked evaluator prompt includes the full GauntletEval adversarial-review instructions from evaluators/gauntlet-eval.md

The emitted script contains the required gauntlet INFO log() calls: batch started (index and item ids), per-round outcome (round number and changed/clean status), converged-at-round-N message, and batch committed (when enable_commits is true)
The emitted script contains ERROR log() calls for: change-detector git failure (treated as changed) and primary or evaluator agent error surfaced for diagnostics
A batch of two items has both items' description, steps, files, specs, and tests present in the baked primary agent prompt and in the baked evaluator agent prompt

Regardless of the implementing.eval.count config value, the emitted evaluator loop spawns exactly one evaluator agent() per round — scripts generated with count=1 and count=4 are equivalent in evaluator fan-out
When max_rounds is 0, the emitted script contains no evaluator loop; the batch is accepted after the primary with a force-accept log line
When min_rounds is 1 and the evaluator changes nothing on round 1, the batch ends after exactly one evaluator round (the floor is satisfied on round 1)
When min_rounds is 0, the emitted script's loop can end on the first unchanged round with no floor; the max_rounds ceiling still bounds the loop
When the evaluator rewrites a file identically (no-op edit), the change-detector's git result is changed=false and the round counts as converged — the evaluator's self-report is not consulted

When the evaluator agent returns null at or beyond min_rounds, the change-detector observes no working-tree change, the round is recorded changed=false, and the batch converges (optimistic); the failure is surfaced at ERROR
When the primary agent returns null, the evaluator loop still runs its rounds against whatever the primary produced; the batch is not aborted
When the change-detector cannot run git, the round is treated conservatively as changed=true, preventing false convergence; an ERROR log line is emitted

The evaluator agent() call in each round uses the baked implementing.eval.model and implementing.eval.type values from config — distinct from the primary's implement.model/implement.type; generating with eval.model/type differing from implement.model/type yields an evaluator call carrying the eval values, not the implement values

When enable_commits is true, commit instructions appear in the baked primary and evaluator prompts and the change-detector's baked instruction commits the accepted batch (the positive counterpart to the enable_commits=false absence case)

The emitted script contains DEBUG log() calls reporting the model/type used for each agent (primary, evaluator, change-detector) and the resolved min_rounds/max_rounds bounds, per the gauntlet Observability DEBUG row

Executing the emitted script against deterministic agent stand-ins (stubbed agent()/log()/phase() with fixed per-round change behavior) for a batch with max_rounds=3 whose evaluator stand-in changes code every round: exactly one primary agent invocation and exactly three evaluator invocations occur — the primary-runs-once invariant

Executing the emitted script against deterministic stand-ins with min_rounds=1, max_rounds=5 and an evaluator stand-in that changes code on round 1 then nothing on round 2: exactly two evaluator rounds run and the batch is recorded converged at round 2

Executing the emitted script against deterministic stand-ins with max_rounds=3 and an evaluator stand-in that changes code on every round: exactly three evaluator rounds run, the batch is accepted in its final state, and a WARN force-accept line is logged — force-accept at ceiling

Executing the emitted script against deterministic stand-ins with min_rounds=2 and an evaluator stand-in that changes nothing on round 1: a second evaluator round still runs before the batch can end — the min_rounds floor is enforced at run time, not merely present in source

items.name: Register generate-workflow CLI command
items.description: Wire forgectl generate-workflow <plan.json> as a cobra subcommand: read and validate the plan using state.ValidatePlanJSON, resolve config via resolveSession, compute batches, render the script, write atomically to .claude/workflows/, and print INFO/WARN/ERROR diagnostics to cmd.OutOrStdout().

tests.description: forgectl generate-workflow plan.json with a valid plan and resolvable config writes exactly one new file under .claude/workflows/ and exits zero, printing the output path and slash-command name
On success the command prints INFO lines for: generation started (plan path), plan validated, and batch count with total item count
A plan path that does not exist exits non-zero with an error naming the path; no file is written

A plan file containing malformed JSON exits non-zero with a parse error that names the offending location (line/column or byte offset); no file is written; this is distinct from a structurally valid but semantically invalid plan
A plan that fails state.ValidatePlanJSON exits non-zero with the validator's diagnostics (same format as forgectl validate); no file is written
When no .forgectl/config is resolvable from the working tree, the command exits non-zero stating config is required; no file is written
When .forgectl/config is present but a required implementing block or field is absent, the command exits non-zero with an error message that names the missing block; no file is written
Two runs against plans differing only in implementing.eval.count (1 vs 4) produce scripts that are equivalent in evaluator fan-out — exactly one evaluator agent() call per round in both scripts
After a successful generation, the plan.json and .forgectl/config files are byte-for-byte unchanged
A mid-write filesystem failure leaves no partial file under .claude/workflows/; the command exits non-zero
At DEBUG verbosity the command logs the resolved config values baked into the script and the per-batch item ids in run order, per the workflow-generation Observability DEBUG row
